  THEIR CERTIFICATES OF                           §
  CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR                   §
  THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH                     §      BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
  TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV                   §
                                                                         OF
  TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN                    §
  BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL,                  §     ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
  LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,                         §

  MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER,                    §

                                   AARON GAMES’S INITIAL BRIEF

         Aaron Games, an affected landowner and intervenor 335, respectfully submits this Initial

Brief. My family’s 48-acre ranch headquarters and home are located directly on Link G13 of the

proposed project.1 I strongly oppose any route that includes Link G13 for the reasons set forth

below.


I. Severe Impacts on My Home and Ranch


         The conductors of the proposed 765 kV transmission line would pass only approximately

115 feet from my house — including my son’s bedroom — with the centerline approximately

175 feet away from my house.2 Prudent avoidance3 dictates that the transmission line run in

excess of 500 feet from residences and other habitable structures, 175 feet from my house, would



         1
             Aaron W. Games Exhibit 1 at 3.
         2
             Id. at 12.
         3
             16 Tex. Admin. Code §25.101(a)(6).
 negligently and grossly fail that test. Here I have taken the time to inform the PUC ALJ of this

issue that the Commission might have failed to consider to this point in time, but this is a

material violation of the PUC’s own rulemaking.


       The easement would take roughly 25% of my 48-acre parcel, while the 500-foot prudent

avoidance zone would affect 60-70% of the property. This drastically reduces the highest and

best use of my land, including future residential development or additional family homes, and

will significantly diminish property value. My home is also mine and my wife’s place of work

and we are here on the property 24 hours a day, seven days a week. My ranching operation

(approximately 75 calves per year plus hay production) depends on living on-site for efficient

daily management of cattle, pastures, and leased lands. The line would require substantial

vegetation clearing and introduce ongoing visual, noise, and potential EMF impacts that would

make continued residence on the property untenable for my family.


II. Inadequate Justification of Need


       The record does not sufficiently establish the need for this specific 765 kV line in this

location. While Permian Basin load growth is cited, the project appears driven largely by

projected demand from large data centers. Affected landowners have not been adequately

consulted on this purpose, and broader alternatives (including technological developments that

could reduce ground-based power demands) have not been fully considered.


III. Public Health and Safety Concerns


       Oncor’s witnesses minimized potential health effects from 765 kV lines, relying on a

claimed lack of conclusive evidence. However, developers routinely avoid siting habitable


                                                 2
 structures within 500 feet of such lines under prudent avoidance principles. Multiple studies have

raised concerns regarding EMF exposure, including possible links to childhood leukemia and

other conditions. As a parent, I refuse to expose my wife, children, or myself to these risks. The

extreme proximity of the conductors to my family’s living spaces directly contravenes the

Commission’s prudent avoidance policy.


       The proposed G13 route poses unacceptable risks to my family’s health and safety. My

primary residence and ranch headquarters at 4018 FM 2657, Briggs, Texas, would lie

approximately 175 feet from the centerline of the proposed line, with my son’s bedroom only

115 feet from the conductor. This extreme proximity raises serious concerns regarding

electromagnetic fields (EMF) and potential health impacts, particularly elevated risks of

childhood leukemia.


       Response to Applicants’ Objections and Motion to Strike EMF/Childhood

       Leukemia Testimony


                  Applicants have objected to portions of my Direct Testimony that reference

       scientific studies and public health concerns regarding EMF exposure from high-voltage

       transmission lines and elevated risks of childhood leukemia. 4 These objections,

       primarily on hearsay and non-expert opinion grounds, should be overruled.


                  1. Hearsay Objections Lack Merit. The cited materials are not random or

       unreliable sources but peer-reviewed epidemiological studies, meta-analyses, and

       authoritative classifications by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).


       4
           Aaron W. Games Exhibit 1 at 7-8.


                                                  3
 IARC classifies extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic fields as Group 2B – possibly

carcinogenic to humans, based primarily on consistent findings of an approximately

doubled risk of childhood leukemia at exposures above ~0.4 μT or in close proximity to

high-voltage lines. Such materials qualify under Texas Rules of Evidence 803(8) (public

records exception) and 803(18) (learned treatises) and are the type of reliable authority on

which a reasonably prudent person relies. SOAH proceedings routinely admit scientific

literature in utility cases involving health and safety. Excluding this evidence would

prevent a complete record on prudent avoidance of potential health impacts—a policy

long recognized by the Commission.


       2. Non-Expert Opinion Objections Mischaracterize the Testimony. I do not

purport to be a medical or EMF expert. As a parent and directly affected landowner, I am

expressing well-founded personal concerns for my family’s health based on publicly

available, widely disseminated scientific information. This is admissible lay opinion

under Tex. R. Evid. 701. Landowner testimony on personal health and safety fears is

routinely accepted in CCN routing cases. Striking it would deny due process and

undermine the Commission’s duty to weigh broad public interest factors under PURA.


       3. Relevance and Weight. The existence of scientific debate and legitimate

public concern regarding EMF and childhood leukemia is highly relevant to route

selection, alternative routes, and the overall public convenience and necessity

determination. Even if any portions were technically challenged, they should be admitted

for the limited purpose of showing the basis of my concerns and the existence of a




                                         4
        genuine public health issue. Commission precedent supports prudent avoidance—

       locating lines farther from residences and family homes where feasible.


       I would like to remind the ALJ and the Commission that these proposed 765 kV

transmission lines are more than 200% more powerful than the previously most powerful

transmission lines in the State of Texas. What I have outlined for you here are findings from

peer reviewed studies and risks. The risks, while significant enough for at least myself, and most

people, would seemingly be more than doubled as well because of the voltage levels and

intimately close proximity of these lines to mine and other people’s residences. These are

unacceptable levels of risk for anyone to take with the health of their families. I find them

unacceptable risks for you to take with the health of my family. I would be shocked that

appointed ALJ, would even consider such risks. Disregarding this evidence in conjunction with

the Commission’s own Prudent Avoidance principles would at least appear to have failed to have

been objective or to have exercised professional care and due diligence. What the ALJ is

considering here are impacts to people’s health and wellbeing. Potentially severely so. For these

reasons, the Administrative Law Judges should give appropriate weight to this evidence in the

Proposal for Decision.


IV. Oncor’s Maintenance and Safety Record


       Oncor has a documented history of serious maintenance failures. This includes multiple

lawsuits involving injuries and deaths related to inadequate vegetation management and line

maintenance, as well as the 2006 Ringgold fire in which Oncor equipment failure led to a blaze

that destroyed approximately 40 homes. These precedents raise grave concerns about placing

additional high-voltage infrastructure near occupied homes and working ranches.


                                                 5
 V. Deficiencies in the Application


       The application uses outdated mapping that omits numerous existing habitable structures

along Link G13. These inaccuracies, which have been documented in multiple intervenor

testimonies (including my own and those from the G-9/G-13 Landowners coalition), undermine

the reliability of the routing analysis and impact assessments.


VI. Conclusion


       For the reasons stated above, I respectfully request that the Commission reject any route

that incorporates Link G13. Alternative routes are available that would avoid these

disproportionate and severe impacts on my family home, ranch operations, and the properties of

similarly situated landowners.


                                              Respectfully submitted,

                                              Aaron Games
